pr_title: e2e framework: replace custom cleanup support with Ginkgo v2 mechanisms
pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

In contrast to ginkgo.AfterEach, ginkgo.DeferCleanup runs the callback in
first-in-last-out order. Using it makes the following test code work as
expected:

    f := framework.NewDefaultFramework("some test")

    ginkgo.AfterEach(func() {
        // do something with f.ClientSet
    })

Previously, f.ClientSet was already set to nil by the framework's cleanup code.

Fixes:  #111979

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
e2e: tests can now register callbacks with ginkgo.BeforeEach/AfterEach/DeferCleanup directly after creating a framework instance and are guaranteed that their code is called after the framework is initialized and before it gets cleaned up. ginkgo.DeferCleanup replaces f.AddAfterEach and AddCleanupAction which got removed to simplify the framework.
```

issue_context.title: e2e: use DeferCleanup for Framework instance
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

The following code is slightly wrong:

```
f := framework.NewDefaultFramework("foo")

AfterEach(func() {
   // do something with f.ClientSet
})
```

It's wrong because f.AfterEach runs first and clear f.ClientSet.

We can make such code work as intended by switching to `DeferCleanup` as discussed in https://github.com/onsi/ginkgo/issues/1022.

### Why is this needed?

Not being able to use the framework instance at the same nesting level is not obvious (causing developers to loose time while debugging a non-working test - been there, done that...) and the workaround (extra Context calls) isn't nice (extra space in test name, more indention).

review_comments: this DeferCleanup seems to be superuseful now that I see how you are using it
will this run twice? we add it to `	f.cleanupHandle = AddCleanupAction(f.AfterEach)` in the next line
it sounds like the thing to remove is the `cleanupHandle` , seems that `DeferCleanup` just fixes https://github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2/issues/222
I think it removes itself once it ran once. But you are right, let's use this opportunity to also remove cleanupHandle.
naive question, do you still need to check if is nil?
No. Because the code now runs only after c was set, it can never be nil.

technical question, should 
```
	// In addition, AfterEach will not be called if a test never gets here.
	ginkgo.DeferCleanup(f.AfterEach)

	// Registered later and thus runs before deleting namespaces.
	ginkgo.DeferCleanup(f.dumpNamespaceInfo)
```

go here , in `NewDefaultFramework`  or inside `BeforeEach()`

The constructor seems the one configuring the hooks order, or do we want the dependency that f.AfterEach only happens if f.BeforeAch has called?

It has to be in `BeforeEach` because `DeferCleanup` is not allowed outside of a `BeforeEach/AfterEach/It` node. That is a somewhat artificial limitation, but conceptually it makes sense: it is meant to be used in combination with some setup code if and only if that setup code actual ran.

That makes sense for us here. If `f.BeforeEach` never gets reached, for example because some earlier `BeforeEach` skipped the test, then there is no need to run `f.AfterEach`.
should we worry about moving from randomised to ordered?

I don't think so. We are not breaking anything ("ordered" is a valid order when previously only "randomized" was guaranteed) and I am not worried about such dependencies actually occurring in practice. Even if they do, the Ginkgo model of deterministic execution would make them okay.
